evidence: M-O s.v. official: high-ranking government official
terms.comment: Properly the office, then the person who holds it (Lewis & Short; see office, a public office): the officials who hold power and decide. For the staff who serve them, see civil servant.

terms.gloss: a junior official, a magistrate’s attendant
evidence: M-O s.v. official: minor government official
terms.comment: The paid staff of the magistrates: lictors, clerks, messengers (Lewis & Short); see civil servant.

evidence: M-O s.v. official: minor government official
terms.comment: A magistrate’s attendant, post-classical for appāritor (Lewis & Short); in later Latin the general word for an official. Levi and Bini (p. 29) give a description, quī mūnere fungitur, one who holds an office.

phrases.latin: Est igitur proprium mūnus magistrātūs intellegere sē gerere persōnam cīvitātis dēbēreque ejus dignitātem et decus sustinēre, servāre lēgēs, jūra discrībere, ea fideī suae commissa meminisse.
phrases.english: It is the proper task of an official, then, to understand that he stands for the state, and must uphold its dignity and honour, keep the laws, give everyone their rights, and remember that these are entrusted to his good faith.

phrases.latin: inter fīlium magistrātum et patrem prīvātum pūblicōs honōrēs cessāre, nātūrālēs et genuīnōs exorīrī
phrases.english: between a son who holds office and a father who is a private citizen, public rank gives way and the rank given by nature comes into force
